full_judgment:
4. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record by judgment and order dated 30th October, 2003 decreed the suit. On appeal, the High Court Division by its judgment and order dated 9th April, 2009 affirmed the judgment. Thereafter the petitioners unsuccessfully moved this Division in Civil Petition Nos.1441 and 1442 of 2009 and then filed this review petition. The High Court Division while maintaining the decree of the trial Court observed that the plaintiffs instituted two suits earlier relating to plot Nos. 1210 and 1216 which plots were said to have been acquired along with suit plot No. 1219 had been decreed, that in those suits the said Gazette Notification has been challenged, that in the present suit as well the said Gazette Notification has been challenged and prayed for release of the suit land and that since earlier suits were decreed it could not take a different view. This Division while maintaining the said judgment observed that the High Court Division rightly held that there was nothing on record to show that the suit land was waqf property and that until and unless the judgments and decrees passed in the earlier suits are set aside, those judgments are binding upon the parties. 

 "I Because the suit land having been acquired and having been notified in the gazette dated 22nd April, 1961 and there being legal bar in challenging acquisition by filing suit and the trial Court and the High Court Division having decreed the suit without taking into consideration of the said legal bar, this Court committed an error of law apparent on the face of the record in dismissing the leave petition and thereby affirming the judgment of the courts below, thus said judgment is required to be reviewed. 

 III. Because this Division affirmed the decree of mandatory injunction passed by the courts below without considering that there is no allegation that the Government made construction on the suit land during the pendency of the instant suit, thus committed an error apparent on the face of record affirming the decree of mandatory injunction and dismissing the leave petition and in the facts of the instant case the judgment passed by this Court requires to be reviewed. 

 IV. Because, admittedly the plaintiffs of the instant suit being not in possession of the suit plot and they having not prayed for recovery of possession, the trial Court as well as the High Court Division is not justified in decreeing the suit without considering the maintainability of the suit and this Division committed error apparent on the face of the record in affirming the same by dismissing the leave petition and as such the judgment passed by the Division required to be reviewed."
